subject: Release timing tradeoffs and triage for 2027Q1 enablement
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, fastcloud-partner@fastcloud.io, acme-trials@acme.com
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0000
Subject: Release timing tradeoffs and triage for 2027Q1 enablement

Team —

We need a decision by EOD Tuesday on whether we shift the Q1 customer-facing rollout for the new inference control surface (the UI + runtime knobs for batching/quantization) into an accelerated Jan window or keep the original March plan.

Context in one line: Acme (trial) is asking for early access in Jan; Partner (FastCloud) is offering a co-marketing slot in Feb if we can show a stable public beta in Jan. That would materially help adoption metrics, but it increases risk on docs, enablement, and regression exposure.

Options I sketched (attached: timeline-options-2027Q1.xlsx):
- Option A — Accelerate: Public beta Jan 15, limited to 3 pilot accounts. Requires reduced feature scope (no per-route autoscale in beta), docs + trainings in two short sprints.
- Option B — Stable launch: keep March 10, full feature set, expanded enablement (train-the-trainer, deep-dive docs).

Asks from each function:
- Eng (Marcus): feasibility + the one or two blockers that would push us past Jan.
- Sales/GTM (Aditya, Monica): which customers must we include in beta for retention/expansion signals?
- PM/Programs (Tessa): enablement lift estimate and critical docs that must land before beta.

Please reply with: a) safe/unsafe for Jan b) top 2 mitigations you need c) owners for the enablement checklist items.

Short attachments: timeline-options-2027Q1.xlsx (proposal), staged-rollout-checklist.md (seed checklist).

Thanks —
Lauren
Senior Director, GTM Enablement
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, acme-trials@acme.com
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Release timing tradeoffs and triage for 2027Q1 enablement

Lauren —

Short answer: Jan is attractive but high-risk from a sales/contracting standpoint. Quick notes:
- Customers: Acme, two pilot SaaS customers (listed in HubSpot HS-ACME-3492) are the ones pushing for Jan. If we do Jan, we should lock an MPS with Acme that clarifies support windows and severity targets for the beta.
- SLAs/Support: We need a documented quick-escalation path (who to loop if an inference outage occurs in pilot). Monica can own that doc.
- Success signals: conversion to paid + observed latency improvements for their production prompts.

Top mitigations: 1) Narrow pilot scope to 3 customers behind feature flags; 2) Defined rollback plan and a pre-approved credit/comp policy for customer impact.

Happy to jump on a 30-min sync tomorrow to align the partner ask.

— Aditya
Account Executive
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 02:18:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Release timing tradeoffs and triage for 2027Q1 enablement

Folks —

Engineering feasibility notes:
- Jan beta is possible but only if we accept a scoped surface: we can deliver the UI controls + backend flags by Jan 15 if we defer per-route autoscale and the new kernel-selection optimizer until March. That reduces integration testing time by ~3 weeks.
- Risk areas: perf regression tests (we need a 48-hour rolling test run against our 4 canonical production prompts) and KV cache migration checks. The perf run will reveal whether quantized kernels introduce any tail-latency regressions.
- Resource ask: need a 0.4 FTE from Infra SREs for one month and a dedicated test node for smoke testing.

I attached a short note on regression risk: perf-risk-notes.pdf. If we proceed, I recommend Option A but with firm gating criteria: no >5% median latency regression and no P95 regressions >15% across canonical prompts.

— Marcus
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 15:07:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Release timing tradeoffs and triage for 2027Q1 enablement

Thanks — pulling together a pragmatic rollout plan and ownership list. Draft below (I'll push to the enablement doc and link to the folder):

Proposed staged rollout (if we pick Jan):
- Phase 0 (Dec 28–Jan 10): internal alpha — docs draft, sales playbook skeleton, internal staging run. Owners: Marcus (tech sign-off), Monica (sales playbook), Lauren (training slots).
- Phase 1 (Jan 15–Feb 15): limited public beta — 3 pilot customers, 2-week feedback window. Owners: Aditya (customer onboarding), Monica (support escalation), Infra SRE (on-call).
- Phase 2 (Feb 16–Mar 10): expanded beta and partner showcase — widen to 10 customers, partner co-marketing assets. Owners: Lauren (partner comms), Tessa (program coordination).

Critical docs to ship before Phase 1: playbook, rollback runbook, customer-facing release notes, support escalation matrix. I'll own the checklist and create a small triage Slack channel for fast ops.

Open questions I need answered for Tuesday decision:
1) Who signs off on the gating metrics when perf tests are complete? (Eng + Product)
2) Is there an approved compensation/credit policy for Pilot outages? (Sales + Finance)
3) Can Infra commit the 0.4 FTE for Jan?

I'll create the staged-rollout-checklist.md and a quick Drive folder by EOD.

— Tessa
Program Manager, Releases
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, fastcloud-partner@fastcloud.io, acme-trials@acme.com
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0000
Subject: Decision: staged public beta (Option A, with gates) — next steps

Team — thanks for the quick turn. Decision: we will proceed with Option A (staged public beta targeting Jan 15) with the following non-negotiable gates. If any gate fails, we revert to the March timeline.

Gating criteria (pass/fail):
- Perf gate: median latency regression <=5% and P95 regression <=15% across canonical prompts (owner: Marcus + Product sign-off).
- Stability gate: no Sev1 regressions in the final 48-hour smoke run (owner: Infra SRE).
- Support gate: escalation matrix and compensation policy documented and approved (owner: Monica + Finance).

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):
- Marcus: run 48-hour perf regression by Jan 6 and publish results to Drive.
- Monica: draft escalation + compensation policy by Dec 27 and share with Sales leadership.
- Tessa: create the pilot onboarding checklist and Slack triage channel by Dec 23.
- Aditya: confirm Acme pilot commitment and sign a scoped MPS by Dec 28.

Links: https://redwood.gdrive/repo/enablement/2027Q1-plan — I will update the decision and the checklist. HubSpot: HS-ACME-3492 is the pilot record.

If any of you foresee a blocker to your assigned item, ping me ASAP — we need visibility by Monday. I'll schedule a 30-min sync for Mon 12/28 to review perf outputs and a final go/no-go.

Thanks —
Lauren
Senior Director, GTM Enablement
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: timeline-options-2027Q1.xlsx, staged-rollout-checklist.md, perf-risk-notes.pdf
